title: ADW Run State
description: One file per ticket. Every stage reads it and writes its own section. The file is the run: if it is not recorded here, it did not happen.

run_id.description: UTC timestamp plus slug: `date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S`-<slug>. UTC so it lines up with the stamps.

source.description: Optional. Where the ticket came from: a user report, an issue link, "self".

base_ref.description: The commit SHA the run started from (`git rev-parse HEAD` at scout). The reviewer diffs against THIS, so it sees every change the run made, committed or not.

stage.description: The stage in progress, or the last one that ran. Set automatically by `adw-stamp.sh <run> <stage> start`. Handover sets "done".

status.description: "in_progress" for the whole run, "passed" once handover closes it, "blocked" when a stage stops it (adw-stamp.sh end ... blocked sets this).

questions_for_human.description: Product decisions the plan must not guess: wording customers see, whether something is required, prices, anything a customer would notice. If non-empty, the run STOPS at plan until the human answers.

by.description: Who answered: a name or a role. A sign-off must say whose it is.

human_decisions.description: The human's answers, word for word, one per question.

challenge.description: One entry per challenge round, appended, never overwritten. `verdict` mirrors the latest round.

mode.description: full = a fresh challenger attacked the whole plan. delta = the SAME challenger checked its own findings were fixed.

exit_code.description: OBSERVED by scripts/adw-gate.sh. Never inferred from output text.

verdict.description: From adw-gate.sh. `suspect` (exit 0 but no proof of work) counts as a failure.

failure_class.description: REQUIRED when the check did not pass. `code` = a real defect, go back to build. `environment` = machine, network or toolchain problem the change cannot fix: fix the environment and RERUN, never skip. `unclassified` = cannot decide yet; treated as a failure until evidence decides it.

failure_evidence.description: The exact output line(s) that justify failure_class. A classification with no quoted line is not a classification.

attempt.description: Which verify attempt produced this check. Re-attempts APPEND new entries; earlier attempts stay as the record.

log_path.description: Full output log (temporary; the output_tail is the durable copy).

attempt.description: Current attempt, starting at 1. Set it BEFORE running the gates; adw-gate.sh --into tags each check with it. "Verify passed" means every check with this attempt number has verdict pass.

reviewed_by.description: `subagent` = judged by a fresh agent that did not write the change. `self` = the same agent reviewed its own work, which is structurally weak and must be recorded as such.

unscoped_findings.description: Behaviour the change introduces that NO acceptance criterion asked for. A finding even when every criterion passes.

diff_lines.description: Lines of change the reviewer actually read. 0 means it reviewed NOTHING, and an approve carrying 0 is rejected.

final_round.description: full = a fresh reviewer read the whole change. delta = the same reviewer checked its flagged items were fixed. Round count comes from history.

review_mode.description: As returned by the reviewer on a delta round. Mirror it into final_round.

review.description: The reviewer's JSON, written exactly as returned. Extra keys the reviewer adds are kept.

history.description: Written ONLY by scripts/adw-stamp.sh (plus the `note` field, which the agent fills in place).

status.description: passed = the stage did its job. waiting = it stopped to ask the human. blocked = the run cannot continue.

terminal_reason.description: REQUIRED once stage is `done` or status is `blocked`. Why the run ended, as a value you can count rather than a story you have to read.

stamps.description: adw-stamp.sh staging area for a stage that has started and not ended. Must be empty or absent on a finished run.

refusals.description: Every point where a stage DECLINED to proceed, whether or not the run later recovered. Append-only; never rewritten when a later attempt succeeds. A loop that never refuses is either well-fed or not looking.

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC from a real `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` call.

unaided.description: TRUE only if no human input preceded the refusal.
